title: A default pool record runs Opus 5.5 on its sanity subset; the full Opus arm runs only when named
goal: run pool with opus-5-5 among its --arms runs that arm on the Opus sanity subset (the kinds csv_fact, multi, synthesis and near_miss, 10 rows, one rep, both effort levels) unless a flag asks for every row, so the record command of benchmarks.md's procedure plans about 20 Opus runs instead of 300 and its dry-run estimate falls by about 60 USD (the 2026-10-09 record: Opus 67.43 USD of 149.74, right in 90.0 percent of runs against 89.3 for Sonnet 5.5 and 84.7 for Haiku 5.5, within the spread); the report's pool tables and 'What it shows' mark the Opus cells that are the subset's and the procedure states that the full Opus arm runs on a model change; pool verify (a) accepts a subset arm whose planned_kinds row names the subset.

run: import subprocess,re,sys;out=subprocess.run(["python3","_tools/benchmarks.py","run","pool","--arms","haiku-5-5,opus-5-5,router","--reps","1","--dry-run"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout;n=sum(int(m) for m in re.findall(r"opus-5-5\S*: (\d+) runs",out));print("opus runs",n);sys.exit(0 if 0<n<=40 else 1)

gates.question: How does a pool run ask for every Opus row instead of the sanity subset: a new flag, or the value all of the existing --arm-kinds (--arm-kinds opus-5-5=all)?

notes: Premise (2026-10-09, benchmark review): the record command's --dry-run plans opus-5-5:low 150 runs (32.62 USD) and opus-5-5:default 150 runs (34.81 USD) of 149.74 USD in all; check 1 fails now (300 runs). The subset is already named by the pool setup (benchmarks.md, the Opus sanity subset: --arms opus-5-5 --kinds csv_fact,multi,synthesis,near_miss --reps 1). No paid run. Premise run at plan (2026-10-09): the dry-run check fails (300 Opus runs planned). report --check and tests.py -k pool pass before the work and pin behaviour that must stay: the subset's cells must keep the report's tables in agreement with the results file and the pool tests green. Ordered after ST-qiep6y7i: both edit the pool section of benchmarks.md.
